errors.permission: You don’t have permission to do that.

errors.alreadyDecided: Someone already decided this request. Reload to see what happened to it.

plans.title: Product catalog
plans.subtitle: What restaurants can buy. Every product carries two prices in USD: one paid once, and one paid every month.
plans.stripeDormant: Stripe is dormant. {count, plural, one {# active product has} other {# active products have}} no Stripe price ID ({codes}). Until every one is filled in, merchants are activated manually from Subscriptions instead of paying by card.

fields.name: Name
fields.includedSeatsHint: Seats the plan grants on its own.
fields.stripePriceIdHint: price_… — required before Stripe can go live.
fields.isQuantity: Quantity product (billed per unit — needs quantity pricing on the Stripe price)
fields.monthlyPriceHint: Charged every month, on top of the one-time price.
fields.oneTimePriceHint: Paid once, ever. 0 for anything sold by the month only.

plans.withdrawnHint: Not on sale. Restaurants already on it keep it and their history still resolves, but nobody new can buy it. Mark it active to sell it again.

reports.title: Financial reports
reports.subtitle: Subscription revenue (your platform income) and platform-wide activity.
reports.activityNote: GMV flows to restaurants (they take payment); driver payouts are settled by restaurants. Your revenue is the subscription MRR above.

settings.title: Platform settings
settings.subtitle: Global configuration for every restaurant on the platform.

penalty.title: Driver penalty
penalty.description: When a driver racks up too many rejects/timeouts in the rolling window, they’re blocked from going online for the cooldown period.
penalty.thresholdHint: Events in the window before a block

tips.title: Delivery tip visibility
tips.description: Controls what a driver sees about the tip on a delivery offer.
tips.legalBody: Hiding the restaurant’s tip cut from drivers may conflict with US tip law (FLSA) and tip-transparency rules in states/cities such as CA, NY, and Seattle, especially for W-2 drivers. Confirm with counsel before enabling in production.

defaults.title: New-branch delivery defaults
defaults.description: Seed values applied when a new branch is created. Branches can override these later. All distances/rates are in miles.

flags.title: Feature flags
flags.description: Turn platform features on or off globally.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.subtitle: Set a restaurant's package directly, branch by branch. Changes take effect immediately.

statusHint.past_due: Past due is a label, not an off switch: the store keeps full access until the paid-through date. Suspend on the dashboard hides the store now; letting the date pass ends access.
statusHint.cancelled: Cancelled is a label, not an off switch: the store keeps full access until the paid-through date. Suspend on the dashboard hides the store now; letting the date pass ends access.
statusHint.expired: Expired ends access as soon as you apply.

subscriptions.blankTrial: Leave blank to restart from today: a {days}-day trial, to {date}.
subscriptions.blankMonth: Leave blank to restart the month from today: paid through becomes {date}.
subscriptions.blankShortens: That is earlier than the current {date}. Pick a date to keep the time they already have.

delivery.title: Which branches deliver
delivery.hint: Every branch that delivers adds the delivery price to the monthly bill. Nothing here charges the one-time unlock — what you grant by hand is not owed.
delivery.trialHint: On a trial every branch delivers, so there is nothing to pick. Move the restaurant to a paid plan to choose.
delivery.noBranches: This restaurant has no branches yet.

subscriptions.noOneTimeCharge: Applying a package here raises no one-time charge.

oneTime.title: Paid once
oneTime.empty: Nothing one-time has ever been charged to this restaurant.
oneTime.unavailable: The one-time ledger could not be read, so this card cannot say what has already been paid. Reload before charging anything.

switches.intro: Show or hide a feature for this restaurant only. Plan follows the package above; On and Off ignore it. Hiding a feature removes it from the merchant’s sidebar; if they open the URL directly they get the locked page instead of the feature.
switches.hiddenNotInPackage: Hidden from the merchant · not in their package
switches.deliveryNote: Delivery is the exception: this switch says the account may have delivery at all, while the branch list above says where. Forcing it On grants nothing until a branch is switched on.

requests.title: Package requests
requests.subtitle: Merchants who chose a package and are waiting to be switched on.
requests.loadFailed: Could not load {name}’s current package, so this card cannot show what approving removes. Approving replaces whatever they have now.
requests.notLive: Not live — the storefront is dark right now
requests.newTotalRequested: New total: {to}/mo (now {from}/mo) · requested at {requested}/mo, today’s catalog prices apply
requests.paidThroughChange: Paid through: {from} → {to}, counted from when you approve
requests.paidThroughChangeFewer: Paid through: {from} → {to}, counted from when you approve ({days, plural, one {# paid day fewer} other {# paid days fewer}})

confirm.blindBody: Their current package could not be loaded. Approving replaces it entirely with this request, removing any add-on or seat the request does not include.
confirm.body: Approving replaces {name}’s whole package with this request.{removes, select, yes { It removes {items}.} other {}}{seats, select, yes { It cuts branch seats from {seatsFrom} to {seatsTo}.} other {}}{shortens, select, yes { It moves paid through back from {paidFrom} to {paidTo} ({days, plural, one {# day fewer} other {# days fewer}}).} other {}} They lose that as soon as you approve, and getting it back means setting the package again on Subscriptions.

requests.unnamedBranches: {count, plural, one {# branch that no longer exists} other {# branches that no longer exist}}
requests.nothingOnce: Nothing to pay once — it is all bought already.
requests.keepsCode: Code {code} stays used — its use was reserved when the merchant sent this request

discounts.title: Discount codes
discounts.subtitle: Codes you hand out. The server prices every one of them.
discounts.oneTimeOnly: Codes come off the one-time charges only — the base, an extra branch, a branch's delivery unlock. They never change the monthly bill.
discounts.emptyBody: Create one when you want to take something off what a restaurant pays to start.
discounts.reservedNote: {amount} more is held on requests waiting for approval.

confirmDeactivate.title: Turn off {code}?
confirmDeactivate.body: Nobody can apply it after this. Requests already sent with it keep their discount when you approve them. It stays on this page with everything it has already given away — a code that has been used is never deleted.

discounts.usesUnavailable: The redemptions for this code could not be read.

form.codeHint: Letters, digits and dashes. Stored upper-case; this is what a merchant types.
form.codeLocked: A code keeps the string it was given away as, so it cannot be renamed.
form.descriptionHint: Shown to the merchant when the code applies.
form.appliesToHint: Pick the one-time charges it comes off. Nothing picked means every one of them.
form.perRestaurantHint: Counted from the redemptions, so a pending request already uses one.
form.startsAtHint: Blank means now. Dates are read in UTC.
form.endsAtHint: Usable through the end of this day, UTC. Blank means no end.

errors.codeCharset: A code can only hold letters, digits and dashes.
errors.codeDuplicate: That code already exists. Pick another one.
errors.valueRequired: Set how much the code takes off.
errors.percentRange: A percent cannot be more than 100.
errors.maxRedemptions: Total uses must be a whole number of 1 or more, or blank.
errors.perRestaurantLimit: Uses per restaurant must be a whole number of 1 or more.
errors.datesBackwards: The end date is before the start date, so the code could never be used.
errors.kindInvalid: The server does not accept that kind of discount.
errors.notFound: That code no longer exists. Reload the page.

errors.managed: This restaurant pays by card through Stripe, so its package only changes through Stripe. Nothing was changed.
errors.paymentInProgress: This change is waiting on the merchant’s card payment at Stripe (3-D Secure or a declined card), and that payment could still go through, so it cannot be rejected yet. It switches on by itself when paid. Once its payment window closes, about a day after it started, it can be rejected. Nothing was changed.
errors.deliveryActive: A branch that delivers is paid for on this restaurant’s card subscription, so Stripe would keep charging delivery for it. The merchant turns delivery off for that branch on their plan page first (that updates Stripe). Nothing was changed.

subscriptions.cancelsLater: Stripe is set to cancel this subscription on {date}. It still renews until then.
subscriptions.pastDue: The last renewal failed. Stripe is retrying the card, and the store keeps working until {date}.
subscriptions.openInvoice: Unpaid invoice: {amount} · {count, plural, one {# attempt} other {# attempts}}
subscriptions.managedNote: Billed by card through Stripe, so there is no package editor here: the package changes when the merchant changes it on their plan page (charged to their card then), and a cancellation or refund is done in Stripe.

requests.subtitle: Merchants who chose a package. Card payments settle by themselves; only requests paid another way wait for you to approve.
requests.awaitingCardNote: The merchant was sent to Stripe’s checkout page to pay this by card. It switches on by itself when Stripe confirms the payment, so there is nothing to approve. Reject it only to clear a checkout they abandoned.
requests.awaitingCardPausedNote: Card payments are switched off, so {name}’s plan page now asks them to send this request to the Favornoms team instead. When they do, it comes back here as an ordinary request for you to approve. Until then it stays here: a checkout they already opened can still be paid, and then it switches on by itself. Reject it only if it should not go ahead.
requests.paymentInProgressNote: {name} is finishing this payment on Stripe’s page: their card needs confirming (3-D Secure) or was declined, so the change waits until it is paid. It switches on by itself once paid. For about a day it cannot be rejected, because the payment could still go through. After that the payment window closes: the request is cleared when the merchant chooses a package again, or you can reject it here.
requests.paymentExpiredNote: Payment window expired — Reject to clear it. {name} did not finish paying this change on Stripe within about a day, so it does not go ahead and nothing changes. If they pay that old invoice anyway, the payment is refunded automatically.
requests.managedRestaurantNote: {name} already pays by card through Stripe, so this change is paid for on their plan page and switches on by itself, whether card billing is switched on or off. It cannot be approved here; reject it only if it should not go ahead.
requests.paidByCardNote: Paid by card on {date}. The package switched on by itself.
requests.rejectBody: Do this only for a checkout the merchant abandoned. If they pay it anyway, the payment is refunded automatically and nothing changes.
requests.rejectExpiredBody: The merchant did not pay this change within Stripe’s payment window. Rejecting clears it and their package stays as it is. If they pay the old invoice anyway, the payment is refunded automatically.

plans.note: Card billing makes its own Stripe prices from the amounts on this page, so no Stripe price ID is needed (<link>Stripe setup</link>). Changing a monthly price creates a new Stripe price: restaurants already paying by card keep their old price until their package changes.
plans.priceIdHint: Not needed any more: card billing finds or creates its Stripe prices from the prices above.

setup.title: Stripe
setup.subtitle: Restaurants pay their package by card into the platform’s own Stripe account. Set it up once for test mode and once for live mode, then switch it on.

load.dormant: The stripe-billing function says Stripe is not set up yet (no secret key). Follow the steps below; this page fills in once the key is saved.
load.notDeployed: The stripe-billing function is not deployed yet, so Stripe’s status cannot be read. The steps below still apply.
load.forbidden: The stripe-billing function refused: only a platform admin can read Stripe’s status.
load.notSignedIn: Your session has expired. Sign in again to read Stripe’s status.
load.network: Couldn’t reach the stripe-billing function. Check your connection and refresh.
load.failed: Could not read Stripe’s status. The steps below still apply.

switch.title: Charge packages by card
switch.onBody: On. A merchant who confirms a package pays by card on Stripe’s checkout page and the package switches on by itself. The monthly fee is charged to the card every month.
switch.offBody: Off. No restaurant starts paying by card: new package requests wait for you on the Requests tab. A request whose card checkout had already started stays “Awaiting card payment” until the merchant pays that checkout or sends the request to the team from their plan page. Restaurants already paying by card keep renewing, can still change their package (charged to their card) and use the customer portal.
switch.unknownBody: Its state cannot be shown until Stripe’s status can be read.

blockers.noStatus: The switch is unavailable until Stripe’s status can be read.
blockers.webhookSecret: Set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET first (Webhook for package payments).

warnings.testMode: Stripe is in test mode: merchants would pay with Stripe’s test cards, no real money moves, and their package still switches on. Switch it on in test mode only to try it yourself.
warnings.chargesOff: Stripe has not enabled payments on this account yet, so checkouts will fail until the account is activated.
warnings.noBank: No bank account for payouts yet: Stripe will collect payments but cannot pay them out.

switch.confirmOnBodyLive: From now on, a merchant who confirms a package is sent to Stripe to pay by card, and the monthly fee renews by itself. Requests already waiting stay on the Requests tab for you.
switch.confirmOnBodyTest: Stripe is in TEST mode. Merchants who confirm a package will be sent to a test checkout: no real money moves, and their package switches on anyway. Only do this to try it yourself.
switch.confirmOffBody: New card purchases stop. Restaurants that do not pay by card yet send their package requests to the Requests tab for you to approve. A request whose card checkout had already started stays “Awaiting card payment” until the merchant pays that checkout or sends the request to the team from their plan page. Restaurants already paying by card are not affected: they keep their Stripe subscription, renew every month until they cancel, and can still change their package by card and use the customer portal.

errors.notReady: Stripe is not ready: set the secret key and the webhook secret first. Nothing was changed.
errors.catalogIncomplete: The Catalog is missing an active monthly price for Base, an extra branch or Delivery, so there is nothing to make the Stripe prices from. Fix it on the Catalog tab first. Card billing was not switched on.
errors.forbidden: Only a platform admin can do this. Nothing was changed.
errors.notSignedIn: Your session has expired. Sign in again, then try the switch. Nothing was changed.
errors.network: Couldn’t reach the server. Nothing was changed — check your connection and try again.
errors.stripeError: Stripe refused while the prices or the customer portal were being prepared, so card billing was not switched on. Try again in a minute.
errors.failed: Could not change the switch. Nothing was changed.
errors.dormant: The stripe-billing function says Stripe is not configured. Nothing was changed.

setup.stepsIntro: Once for test mode and once for live mode. Each step links to the page in Stripe where it is done.

account.title: Stripe account connected
account.body: The secret key (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in the Supabase secrets) connects the platform to your Stripe account. A key starting sk_test_ is test mode; sk_live_ is live.
account.connected: {id} · {mode, select, live {live mode} test {test mode} other {mode unknown}}
account.noAnswer: The key is set but Stripe did not answer — it may be wrong or revoked.

publishableKey.title: Publishable key
publishableKey.body: STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in the Supabase secrets. Package payments use Stripe’s own checkout page, so this one is for completeness.

activation.title: Account activated
activation.body: Stripe needs your business details before the account can take payments and pay out.
activation.due: {count, plural, one {Stripe needs # more detail} other {Stripe needs # more details}} before it activates the account.
activation.chargesOff: Stripe has not enabled payments on this account yet.
activation.payoutsOff: Payouts are paused until Stripe has what it needs.
activation.testMode: Test mode needs none: Stripe’s test cards work before the account is activated. Activate it before going live.

bank.title: Bank account for payouts
bank.body: Where Stripe pays the package money out to you.
bank.missing: No bank account on file yet.
bank.testMode: Test mode needs none. Add one before going live.

webhook.title: Webhook for package payments
webhook.body: Stripe tells the platform through this webhook when a package is paid, renewed or fails. Without it, no card payment switches a package on.
webhook.noEventYet: No event received yet — Stripe sends the first one when a merchant pays.

retries.title: Failed-payment retries
retries.body: In Stripe, Billing → Revenue recovery → Retries. A restaurant keeps working for 7 days after a failed renewal while Stripe retries the card, so Stripe has to give up within that week and then cancel the subscription: a longer retry window would keep charging a card after the store has gone dark. This page cannot read that setting.
retries.setting: Set Smart Retries to retry within 1 week, and when all retries for a payment fail, cancel the subscription.

prices.title: Prices in Stripe
prices.body: Made from the Catalog’s monthly prices.
prices.auto: Made automatically when you switch card billing on.
prices.missingWhileOn: Card billing is on but the prices are missing. Switch it off and on again to recreate them.

portal.title: Customer portal
portal.body: Where merchants update their card, see their invoices and cancel at the end of the paid month. Plan changes stay on the Favornoms plan page.
portal.auto: Set up automatically when you switch card billing on.
portal.missingWhileOn: Card billing is on but the portal is not set up. Switch it off and on again to set it up.

webhook.how1: In Stripe, open Workbench → Webhooks and create a new destination.
webhook.how2: Events from: Your account. API version: {version} if offered. Payload: snapshot, not thin events.
webhook.how3: Tick the {count} events below — no others.
webhook.how4: Destination type: Webhook endpoint. Paste the endpoint URL below.
webhook.how5: Open the new destination, reveal its signing secret (whsec_…) and save it in Supabase as the secret STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
webhook.notConnect: This is not the webhook for diners’ card payments (Connect). That one has its own destination and its own secret; do not reuse it.

copy.failed: Select and copy it by hand

events.title: Recent package-payment events
events.subtitle: From the Stripe webhook and the card-payment code, newest first, times in UTC. Diners’ card payments (Connect) are not listed.

types.settleFailed: Paid, but the package could not be applied
